name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Security Deposit Withholding Dispute with Landlord in Bengaluru
case_dossier.summary: The tenant vacated the 2BHK flat in Bengaluru after providing proper notice and clearing all utility bills, but the landlord has wrongfully withheld Rs 45,000 from the security deposit under the pretext of repainting and deep cleaning for normal wear and tear.

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
Your dispute with your landlord over the withholding of your security deposit is a civil matter governed by your rental agreement and state rent laws. Under Indian law, routine wear and tear of a property cannot be used as a valid excuse by a landlord to make deductions from your security deposit. You hold strong evidence, including move-in and move-out media and WhatsApp acknowledgments, to support your claim for a full refund.

Key Legal Standing: The Transfer of Property Act protects you from unjustified charges for normal wear and tear when returning possession of a property. Mere failure to refund a deposit is a civil dispute and not a criminal offense.

Immediate Takeaway: Gather your lease agreement, bank statements, and chat records, and serve a formal written demand notice to your landlord to initiate the recovery process.

governing_laws.relevance: Protects you by establishing that a tenant is only required to return the property subject to changes caused by reasonable wear and tear, shielding you from unjustified repainting and cleaning deductions.
Affirms your duty to hand over possession, which you successfully fulfilled by returning the keys and clearing utility dues.

action_options.title: Serve Formal Legal Notice
action_options.details: Send a formal written legal notice to your landlord demanding the full refund of the withheld Rs 45,000 security deposit. Clearly cite Section 108(B)(m) to dispute unauthorized wear-and-tear deductions, attaching your move-in/move-out evidence and WhatsApp chat acknowledgments.

action_options.title: Seek Free Legal Guidance via DLSA
action_options.details: Contact the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) via Helpline 15100 for free legal guidance and support. Note: DLSA provides free legal aid and guidance only; it is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against a landlord.

action_options.title: File a Civil Recovery Suit
action_options.details: If the landlord fails to respond or refund the amount after the notice period, file a recovery suit or application before the local civil court / Small Causes Court in Bengaluru based on your rental agreement and state rent regulations.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: For filing a civil recovery suit in a local civil court or Small Causes Court, consulting or engaging a licensed advocate is recommended to properly draft pleadings and represent your case.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR WRONGFUL WITHHOLDING OF SECURITY DEPOSIT AMOUNTING TO RS 45,000 IN RESPECT OF PREMISES LOCATED AT HSR LAYOUT, BENGALURU.**

Sir,

I, am a resident of Bengaluru and was a tenant occupying your 2BHK flat located in HSR Layout, Bengaluru (hereinafter referred to as the "Scheduled Premises"). I hereby issue this legal demand notice to you, Mr. Ramesh, calling upon you to refund the wrongfully withheld security deposit of Rs 45,000, as per the facts and legal standing detailed below:

### FACTUAL SEQUENCE OF EVENTS

1. That 2 years prior, I entered into a tenancy arrangement with you for the Scheduled Premises at a monthly rent of Rs 28,000, and paid a security deposit of Rs 1,00,000 at the commencement of the tenancy.
2. That on 1st October, I duly served a proper 1-month notice to vacate the Scheduled Premises, in accordance with our rental terms.
3. That on 31st October 2024, I successfully vacated the Scheduled Premises, cleared all pending electricity and water utility bills, and formally handed over the keys to you.
4. That 3 days post-vacation, you inspected the premises and promised to refund my security deposit via UPI.
5. That 25 days later (Yesterday), you abruptly stopped picking up my phone calls and sent a text message stating that you were deducting Rs 45,000 from my security deposit for house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

### VIOLATION OF STATUTORY PROVISIONS AND TERMS

1. I state and submit that your deduction of Rs 45,000 under the pretext of repainting and deep cleaning is completely unjustified and arbitrary. Under Section 108(B)(m) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is only required to return the property subject to changes caused by reasonable wear and tear, and cannot be held liable to bear the costs of routine wear and tear or general maintenance like repainting and polishing upon vacating.
2. I have duly fulfilled my obligation under Section 108(B)(q) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, by peacefully returning possession of the property after clearing all utility dues.
3. Furthermore, I hold contemporaneous evidence, including move-in photos, a move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat records where you explicitly acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition.

### DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION

Therefore, through this notice, I hereby call upon you to refund the wrongfully withheld security deposit amount of **Rs 45,000** to my bank account within a suggested 15-day period (customary pre-litigation practice) from the date of receipt of this notice. 

The bank account details for the transfer are as follows: 
- **Account Holder Name:** [Your Name] 
- **Bank Name:** [Your Bank Name] 
- **Account Number:** [Your Account Number] 
- **IFSC Code:** [Your IFSC Code] 

### WARNING OF FURTHER LEGAL ACTION

Please take notice that if you fail to refund the aforementioned sum of Rs 45,000 within the suggested 15-day period, I shall be constrained to initiate appropriate legal proceedings. This will include filing a civil recovery suit or application before the local civil court / Small Causes Court in Bengaluru to recover the principal amount along with costs, and seeking guidance from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA Helpline: 15100) for free legal support, entirely at your risk, cost, and consequences.

A copy of this notice is retained in my records for further necessary action.

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name] 

---

### ANNEXURE INVENTORY
1. Copy of the Original Lease / Rental Agreement
2. Receipt of Security Deposit Payment
3. Move-in Photographs
4. Move-out Handover Video
5. All Rent Payment Bank Statements
6. Screenshots of WhatsApp Chat Acknowledging Property Condition

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre, Section-wection kya bol rahe ho ji! Agreement padha hai kya tune? Clause 14 mein clearly likha hai flat pristine condition mein hand over karna padega. Deep cleaning aur painting ka kharcha toh tenant ko hi dena padta hai. Video dikhane se kuch nahi hota, market mein painting ka rate pata hai kya tumhe?

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You successfully cited Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, along with concrete evidence like the handover video and chat proofs.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Maintain your ground on the exact deadline. While you mentioned 7 days, firmly reiterate that withholding deposit for normal wear and tear without itemized damage proof is legally untenable.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Mr. Ramesh, the handover video clearly proves there is only normal wear and tear, which is legally excluded from deductions, so please transfer the Rs 45,000 immediately.
